subject: Maths
title: Adding and subtracting vectors
subtitle: Vectors · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can add and subtract column vectors and represent the results on a grid.

key_vocab.definition: A vector has magnitude and direction, written as a column vector. To add vectors, add the corresponding components. To subtract, subtract components.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract column vectors and represent the results on a grid.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: vector -- A vector has magnitude and direction, written as a column vector. To add vectors, add the corresponding components. To subtract, subtract components.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Add or subtract the x-components and y-components separately.
(a, b) + (c, d) = (a+c, b+d)
Component-wise addition

Key examples:
  ✓ (3, 2) + (1, 4) = (4, 6)  (add components)
  ✓ (5, 3) - (2, 1) = (3, 2)  (subtract components)
  ✓ a + b means travel along a then along b  (triangle rule)
  ✗ (3, 2) + (1, 4) = (4, 8)  (add each component separately)
  ✗ (5, 3) - (2, 1) = (3, 4)  (subtract y from y, not add)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – adding two vectors
  Find (3, 2) + (4, -1).
  Add x-components: 3 + 4 = 7
  Add y-components: 2 + (-1) = 1
  Result: (7, 1)
  (7, 1)
  (Add each component separately.)

Example 2 – subtracting vectors
  Find (5, 6) - (2, 4).
  Subtract x-components: 5 - 2 = 3
  Subtract y-components: 6 - 4 = 2
  Result: (3, 2)
  (3, 2)
  (Subtract each component separately.)

sections.title: Finding unknown vectors
sections.content:
Find the unknown vector.

(a) a + (3, 2) = (7, 5). Find a.
(b) (5, 1) + b = (2, 6). Find b.
(c) a - (2, 3) = (1, -1). Find a.
(d) (4, 7) - b = (1, 3). Find b.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ (3, 2) + (1, 4) = (4, 6)
✗ (3, 2) + (1, 4) = (4, 8)
✓ Subtracting a vector reverses its direction
✗ (5, 3) - (2, 1) = (3, 4)
✓ The zero vector (0, 0) is the result when a vector is subtracted from itself
